column2: By that fire the pierced navel — diseases and seizers perish. The discus is yellow, the mace red, the vowels dark, the interval dark;
the rim white outside, a black-colored line and the earthly; in the middle and the other spokes the colors — thus one should draw two wheels.
First having brought the water-pot and set it in the range, having given Sudarshana, one should offer in order in the southern wheel:
ghee, apamarga fuel, unbroken rice, sesame and mustard, pudding, cow-ghee, by the count of eight thousand;
the knower of the rule should cast the remnant of the oblation into the pot with each substance; the lump made by the prastha measure one should place in that pot;

Vishnu and all one should place there, and there on the right: "Homage to the servants of Vishnu, makers of all peace; accept for peace, homage" — with this mantra one should give the offering with the water of the oblation remnant.
In a vessel arranged with a board, palasha of the milk-tree, having placed it filled with cow-products, in the directions thus one should have Brahmins offer;
these two oblations with fee destroy spirits and the like. Minor troubles are removed by leafless ones written on leaves smeared with cow-products;
with durva for life, with lotuses for prosperity, with udumbara for sons; for success in cattle with ghee in the cow-pen; for intelligence with all trees.

Om kshraum, homage to the Lord Narasimha, garlanded with flames, with blazing fangs, fire-eyed, destroyer of all demons, destroyer of all beings, destroyer of all fevers, burn burn, cook cook, protect protect, hum phat — this mantra of Narasimha wards off all troubles; by recitation and the rest it removes minor seizers, epidemics, poisons and diseases. A powder with frog and age makes water and fire stop.
Vishnu, with copper eyes rolling with intoxication, generous, bewildered by Kama, adorned with divine garlands, garments and ointment, smiling-faced,
with a retinue of various kinds, gracious, the benefactor of the worlds, with the splendor of a thousand suns,
bearing five arrows, with eyes having attained desire, two- or four-armed, surrounded by divine women, eyes fixed on the Goddess's face — one should recite.
One should worship him holding discus, conch, bow, sword, mace, pestle, goad and noose, from invocation to dismissal;
Shri seated on the left thigh and shank, embracing her husband with her hand, with lotus and chowrie in hand, stout, with Shrivatsa and Kaustubha;

one should worship Hari garlanded, in yellow garments, rich in discus and the rest. "Om Sudarshana, great king of discs, terrifier of the wicked, cut, phat; Om to the water-dweller svaha; sharp sword, cut cut; homage to the sword; to Sarnga with arrows hum phat; we know the group of beings, we meditate on the fourfold; may that Brahman impel us; Samvartaka, Shvasana, crush crush hum phat svaha; noose, bind bind, draw draw hum phat; with goad cut hum phat" — in order on the arms with these own mantras one should worship the weapons.
Om to the king of birds hrum phat — one should worship Tarkshya on the pericarp, the limb-gods by rule; the powers in the Indra and other diagrams, Tarkshya and the rest holding chowries;
the powers should be applied at the end and beginning, the lords of gods and the rest with Dandin. In the yellow, Lakshmi and Sarasvati; Rati, Priti and Jaya white;
Kirti and Kanti in white and dark; Tushti and Pushti arisen by Smara; one should worship the god Vishnu up to the world-lords for success of desired aims.

One should meditate, recite this mantra, offer, and consecrate: "Om shrim krim hrim hum, homage to Vishnu the bewilderer of the three worlds" — by this worship and the rest one obtains all desires as before.
With waters, the bewilderer; with flowers one should daily satisfy him. Brahma with Shakra, Shri and Dandin: the seed of Trailokyamohana;
having recited three lakh and offered a lakh with bilva and ghee, with rice, fruit, scents and the rest, with durva one obtains life;

pleased with consecration, oblation and the rest, he gives the desired. "Om homage to the Lord Varaha, lord of bhur, bhuvah, svah: give me lordship of the earth — svaha to the heart"; five-limbed; having recited ten thousand daily, one obtains the kingdom of life.
With raised hand holding a red lotus, one should meditate on the white-limbed Vanamalini at the south door;
one should meditate on the green one lifting a white lotus upward with both arms, named Vibhishika, Shri's messenger, at the west door;
Shankari at the north door; in the middle of them an eight-petal lotus: Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha
are to be meditated on the lotus petals bearing conch, discus and mace, with the glow of collyrium, milk, saffron and gold, well clothed.
On the petals in the southeast and the rest: Guggulu, Kurunthaka, Damaka and Salila — elephants shining like silver,
bearing golden pots; and on the pericarp one should remember Shri, four-armed, golden, with lotus in two upraised arms,
right hand in fearlessness, left giving boons, in white scent and cloth, bearing a single silver garland and weapon;
having meditated on her with her retinue and worshipped, one obtains everything. One should not wear on the head leaves of drona, lotus flower or shrivriksha;
salt and amalaka are to be avoided on the tithi days in order. Eating pudding, one should recite the Shri hymn and consecrate her with it;
having meditated on the head, from invocation to dismissal, one should worship Shri. With bilva, ghee, lotus and pudding separately the combination is for prosperity.

Poison, buffalo-beloved, fire, Rudra, light, two herons: "Om hrim, great buffalo-crusher, tha tha — root mantra — homage to the buffalo-slayer; make the buffalo-enemy wander wander hum phat tha tha; make the buffalo neigh, hum; kill the buffalo, goddess, hum, buffalo-destroyer phat" — the Durga heart is told with limbs, accomplishing all aims.

One should worship that goddess as told, and the seat in the middle of the limbs. "Om hrim, Durge, protector, svaha" and "homage to Durga"; "homage to the excellent-colored," "to Arya, to golden-radiant, to Krittika, to giver of fearlessness, to maiden, to beautiful" — one should worship these forms standing on petals with the first vowels in order.
To the discus, conch, mace, sword, bow, arrow. On the eighth and other tithis one should worship this Durga up to the world-lords. Durga-yoga gives life, prosperity, a master, victory and the like.
With the mantra of Ishana in concentration, sesame oblation brings control; with lotuses victory; with durva peace; with palasha desire;
with crow's feather nourishment; death and hatred may result. The mantra removes all fear of Brahmins' wrath and minor dangers.
Om Durge Durge, protector, svaha is the protecting mantra told, with the limbs of Jaya-Durga. Having meditated on the dark three-eyed goddess, oneself four-armed,
bearing conch, discus, lotus, trident and the rest, in terrible form; one should arrange it at the start of battle, worship it for victory in sword-work and the rest.
With peacock bracelets, crest of feathers, with sprout-like clothes, seated on a lion throne, with a peacock-feather umbrella,
three-eyed, dark, the goddess adorned with forest-garland, with a snake-ear ornament, with armlets,
with a serpent girdle, with anklets made of snakes — having become so in form, one should recite her mantra a hundred thousand times.
Ishvara in the past became a Kirata form, and Gauri likewise; one should recite, meditate and worship her, removing poison and the rest, for all success.
On an eight-lion throne she is to be worshipped on the petals in the east and so on in order; the limb-Gayatri is declared; at the petal tips "hum"-sounds;
and "phat-kari" in front of the goddess; one should worship these with the Shri seed. They have the colors of the world-guardians' weapons; "Phat-kari" bearing the bow.
Jaya and Vijaya at the door-keepers' places with golden staffs are to be worshipped; Kinkara, Barbari, Mundi and Laguli outside them.
Having worshipped thus one succeeds with substances; in a pit of yoni shape one should offer. With arjuna grains gold is gained; with wheat, nourishment and wealth;
with barley, grains and sesame all success and destruction of calamity; with akshas madness of the enemy; with shalmali, killing;
with jambu, wealth and grain; satisfaction with blue lotuses; with red lotuses great nourishment; with kunda flowers great rise;
with jasmine disturbance of the city; with water lilies the people's love; with ashoka a son; with patala an auspicious woman;
with mango life; with sesame prosperity; with bilva Shri; with champaka wealth; with madhuka flowers and bilva one obtains omniscience.
By three lakh recitations, all attainment, by oblation, meditation and worship likewise; having worshipped in the mandala, twenty-five oblations with the Gayatri
one should give; three hundred from the root; with sprouts one becomes initiated. Having first drunk the five cow-products one should always eat the cooked offering.
Tala and the seven nether worlds, the Kalagni and the end of the worlds; from Omkara and the vowels up to what denotes the cosmic egg,
from Omkara one should whirl the water; then Totala, Tvarita. I shall tell the prelude: one should write the group of vowels on the ground:
the palatal group is the ka-group; the third is tongue-palate; the fourth is palate-tongue-tip; the fifth is tongue-teeth;
the sixth is endowed with eight pouches; the seventh is the mixed group; the sibilants are the sha-group; then one should extract the mantra.
Mounted on the sixth vowel, ending with a sibilant, with bindu; the second of the palatal group joined with the eleven vowels;
the union of tongue and palate is first alone; that same second one should place below;
joined with the eleven vowels, the first from the palatal group; the second of the sibilant one should place below, seen;
the second of the sibilant joined with sixteen vowels; in the union of tongue-teeth one should place the first below;
the second from the mixed group again below; split by the fourth vowel, joined with the palatal group and the rest;
the second of the sibilant one should place below; split by the eleven vowels, ending with a sibilant, with bindu;
mounted on the five vowels by closing of the lips; the second letter, and the other at the tongue-tip with the palate;
the first to be joined in the fifth; these are extracted with half a vowel. Beginning with Om and ending with "namah," one should recite with "svaha" in the fire rite.

Om hrim hrum hrah is the heart; "ham, hrim" the head; "hrim jvala" the crest; the armor the two jaws; "hrim shrim kshum" for the three eyes — the knowledge-eye is declared; "kshaum hah khaum hum phat" for the weapon; one should place the secret limbs before. I shall tell the Tvarita limbs; hear from me the knowledge-limbs: the first two is the heart, three-four the head,
five-six the crest, seven-eight the armor, the eye is the Taraka; the sign is nine and a half syllables.
Totala is declared; then in "vajratunde"; "kha kha hum" is ten-seeded; Vajratunda Indradrutika;
Khechari, Jvalini, Jvale kha kha — Jvalini ten; "Varche, Sharavibhishani kha kha" and Shavari too;
Che, Chhedani, Karalini kha kha and Karali too; "chest-flowing, speed-leaping, kha kha" messenger-leap;
woman-child-maker, shaker, Shastri, Vasana-vegika; kshe paksha Kapile, hasa hasa — Kapila is the messenger by name;
hrum, Tejovati, Raudri and Matanga-Raudri messenger; "puta puta kha kha, sword, phat" Brahmaka messenger;
Vaitalini — ten syllables; abandon the others like chaff of the snake-skin. In the placing beginning with the heart and the rest, the wise should place in the middle on the eye;
from the feet to the head, from the head to the feet; at feet, knees, thighs, private part, and from the navel, heart and throat region.
